title: SwingAI analysis result
description: What an analyzer concluded about one captured shot. Written by the Python analysis pipeline, read by the Rust runtime. Times are integer nanoseconds on the same capture-session clock as the capture manifest for the same shot_id; see docs/adr/0001-hybrid-rust-python-runtime.md.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Only the exact supported version is accepted; there is no minor-version compatibility yet, so writer and reader move together.

shot_id.description: The shot this result describes. Matches the capture manifest, and obeys the same identifier rules — an id one document accepts and the other rejects could not be matched up at all.

analyzer.description: Which analyzer produced this. Results are only comparable within one name+version.

created_at.description: Wall-clock time the analysis finished. For humans and filing only.

status.description: ok: everything asked for was produced, and errors is empty. partial: usable output with something missing — see warnings. failed: no usable output; events may be empty.

events.description: Detected swing events, e.g. the P-positions. May be empty when status is failed.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems. Present output is still usable.

errors.description: Fatal problems. Must be empty when status is "ok".

measurements.description: Scalar measurements keyed by name, e.g. "tempo_ratio" or "backswing_duration_ms". Deliberately a flat open map — biomechanics is not modelled here yet.

artifacts.description: Files the analysis produced, such as an overlay render or a chart.

schemaVersion.description: The only version this contract revision defines. A later ADR may introduce minor-version compatibility; until then a mismatch is an error rather than a partial read.

identifier.description: A shot identifier. Must be usable verbatim as a directory name on every host SwingAI runs on, so the rules are Windows' — the booth is a Windows machine and a shot folder is meant to be copied between hosts, so the stricter platform sets the rule. Rejected: / \ : * ? " < > | and control characters; "." and ".."; a trailing period or space, which Windows silently strips, so "shot." and "shot" would name one directory; and the reserved DOS device names CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-COM9 and LPT1-LPT9 in any case, with or without an extension, because "nul.capture" still names the null device. These mirror the rules swingai-core's ShotId and CameraId enforce; the two sides of the seam must not disagree about what an id may be.

rfc3339DateTime.description: An RFC 3339 date-time, e.g. "2026-07-31T14:22:05.412Z" or "2026-07-31T16:22:05.412+02:00". An offset is required. The pattern is present as well as "format" because most JSON Schema validators treat "format" as an annotation unless a format checker is installed. The pattern is structural only — it cannot reject an impossible calendar date such as 2026-02-30, which the Rust implementation does.

timestampNs.description: Nanoseconds since the capture session's monotonic origin, the same clock as the capture manifest for this shot_id. The persisted origin is zero, so values are session-relative and are only comparable within one session. Nonnegative because nothing in a session precedes its own origin.

relativePath.description: Forward-slash path relative to the directory containing this result, e.g. "artifacts/overlay.mp4". Host-independent: backslashes are rejected outright on every platform, which also rules out C:\..., UNC \\server\share, extended-length \\?\C:\..., and rooted \... spellings. Must not be absolute, must not name a drive, and must not escape the directory with "..".

swingEvent.description: One detected instant in the swing.

name.description: Event label, e.g. "P1" or "impact". Free-form on purpose: the two Python detection paths disagree about whether the velocity peak is P6 or P7 (see CLAUDE.md), and this contract does not adjudicate that.

timestamp_ns.description: The analyzer's best estimate of when the event happened.

range.description: Plausible bounds on the event. Must contain timestamp_ns.

metadata.description: Analyzer-specific extras (which view resolved it, which rule fired). Opaque to the contract; round-tripped unchanged.

kind.description: What this file is, e.g. "overlay_video" or "chart". Open set.
